prompt:
You receive 2 images. Image 1 is a finished background painting of our point-and-click adventure game: the summit plateau of Chopok east of the Rotunda, with the fictional Atlas pavilion, painted in summer 2035. Image 2 is the same painting with coloured boxes that only mark the interactive objects, the exits and the walkable floor, which must all stay exactly where they are. Edit image 1 into the SAME PLACE on 6 February 2035, a clear cold day in deep winter, seen by the SAME CAMERA: keep the exact viewpoint, lens, horizon, perspective and framing, and keep the position, size and outline of every building, wall, door, window, pole, rail, sign, piece of furniture, object and tree trunk. Change only what winter changes, as described below. Keep the painting technique, brushwork, palette handling and level of detail of image 1.

Winter changes (Chopok summit plateau, about 2000 m, in deep winter):
- The whole plateau is under deep, wind-shaped snow: smooth white drifts instead of the gravel, rocks and grass; the
  dwarf pines left, right and behind the path are rounded snow-covered mounds with a few dark green needles showing;
  the rocks are white humps.
- The Rotunda complex keeps exactly its shape, size and position: the stone drum with the glass top and the red ring
  roof, the two long dark station wings on stilts, the steel stairs, the stone base with the ROTUNDA CHOPOK lettering
  (keep the lettering exactly). Thick snow lies on the red ring roof and on the flat roofs of both wings; white rime
  ice coats the railings, the stilts, the steel stairs and the lift pylon at the left; icicles hang from the wings.
- The lift pylon at the left carries the cable-car ropes with one cabin on them.
- The distant mountain ridges on the horizon are white winter mountains.
- The Atlas pavilion on the right keeps its larch boards and white panels; a thick cushion of snow lies on its flat
  roof edge with icicles hanging from it, and a small drift lies along its foot. The open service bay stays open and
  clear: the rugged terminal on its cart (the box labelled 'Servisný terminál' in image 2 (x 1280-1430, y 520-690 of the 1920x1080 frame (67-74 % from the left, 48-64 % from the top))) with its glowing blue screen stays exactly the same;
  the taped paper note (the box labelled 'Papierová poznámka' in image 2 (x 1495-1569, y 462-546 of the 1920x1080 frame (78-82 % from the left, 43-51 % from the top))) stays the same (scribbles only); the orange-black cable bundle
  (the box labelled 'Káble' in image 2 (x 975-1440, y 690-782 of the 1920x1080 frame (51-75 % from the left, 64-72 % from the top))) lies clearly visible ON TOP of the packed snow, running from the bay to the junction box.
- Sky: clear deep winter blue with one or two small clouds; low sun; sparkle on the snow; a little spindrift blowing
  off the crest of a drift.

Walkable floor: the band at x 300-1790, y 626-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (16-93 % from the left, 58-94 % from the top) is a cleared, trodden path of packed snow (white, with footprints), ONE continuous flat open
surface: no rocks, no drifts, no banks and nothing standing in it; the deep snow and the drifts lie only beside it.
Exits: the box labelled 'exit: Chopok pri Rotunde' in image 2 (x 600-720, y 470-600 of the 1920x1080 frame (31-38 % from the left, 44-56 % from the top)) is the Rotunda entrance in the stone base, cleared of snow; the box labelled 'exit: Vyhliadková terasa pri Rotunde' in image 2 (x 400-550, y 380-610 of the 1920x1080 frame (21-29 % from the left, 35-56 % from the top)) is the steel
stairs on the left wing with snow on the steps; the box labelled 'exit: Chronokomora pavilónu Atlas' in image 2 (x 1615-1785, y 420-765 of the 1920x1080 frame (84-93 % from the left, 39-71 % from the top)) is the pavilion door.
This room has no NPC zones.

Fiction rules: keep the ROTUNDA CHOPOK lettering; no other new lettering, no logos, no people, no animals.

Image 2 is a positioning aid only: do NOT draw any of its boxes, outlines, labels or captions. The result is image 1 edited, in the same 16:9 framing: no frames, no borders, no UI, no captions, no watermark, no text except the lettering already in image 1, and no people or animals unless stated above.

Lighting: a clear, cold, sunny winter day in the Low Tatras mountains: deep clean blue sky, low winter sun, crisp blue-violet shadows on the snow, sparkle on fresh snow, cold bright air. The brushwork, line quality and palette harmony stay exactly those of image 1 (style A).

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.

blocking.note: The fictional Atlas service pavilion on the real gravel plateau ~50 m east of the Rotunda (DECISIONS item 6), painted as its exterior with the open service bay (orchestrator brief: S48 exterior, S49 interior). Camera ~1.7 m high on the plateau, looking west at the Rotunda complex as in the 2016 photos taken from the summit path; horizon y ~470; the Rotunda's entrance and its external steel stairs stand far back on y ~560, the pavilion's front on the right stands on y ~765 (~160 px per metre there). Perspective s(y) = (y - 470) / 545. Left/centre: the Rotunda (stone base, red band with the lettering ROTUNDA CHOPOK, glass drum, red ring roof) between the dark station wings, the steel stairs up to the roof terrace; the gravel plateau with rocks, dwarf pine and June snow patches; right: the modular timber-and-white pavilion of the exhibition with its open service bay (terminal on a rugged cart, a taped paper note beside it, cables on the gravel) and the door to the inner chamber. The walk polygon follows the open gravel path only: the dwarf pine, the rocks and the snow patches of the painting on both sides of the path stay outside it; in front of the pavilion door it is a narrow strip.
